name: character_crowd
title: Character Crowd, the NextGeo total against skinned Nanite (GN-5's parent)

lines.name: Character Crowd NextGeo total (GN-5's parent)
lines.reason: Provisional UE group: the four GPU columns that appear in the capture only when the meshes are Nanite (a names-only comparison with the same map's meshes imported without Nanite, on the RTX 4080 SUPER machine in game mode); Nanite's virtual shadow map raster runs inside GPU/ShadowDepths with the rest of the shadow work and is left out. The settings record names the final columns (plan §23.5). With Nanite on, the walkers leave the base pass while GPU/GPUSkinCache stays active, so part of the skinning still runs there; whether that column belongs in the total is open too. The GodotNext group is not defined: the generated PN scene carries no NextGeo virtual geometry (its meshes are procedural ArrayMeshes, and NextGeo builds virtual geometry only at import), and the PN features this line measures are not built yet, so a GodotNext timing run of it has no NextGeo cull or raster column. The UE map places the 100 walkers as skeletal mesh actors of one Nanite-enabled skeletal mesh, each playing a clip of the poses GodotNext showed on every row; the skeletal mesh's own material slot holds the port's material, because with the importer's material there the walkers drew through GPU/Basepass as in the Nanite-off map (a material without the usage flag its mesh needs is replaced by the default material, Epic's Material Properties page says; the runner now fails such a run).
